title: Nonnegative average complexity
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\Omega$ be a finite input alphabet with probability distribution $\\pi$, let $\\alpha$ be an output set, and let $f:\\Omega^n\\to\\alpha$. The infimum of the average query costs, under independent inputs drawn from $\\pi$, of all finite randomized decision trees that compute $f$ is nonnegative.
hypotheses_covered: $\\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\\Omega$
